item.description: Having mapped a cell complex X=(X_\bullet,\phi _\bullet) into a cellular chain complex C_\bullet, we can perform a homological study on the latter.

item.description: Modules are a generalization of vector spaces. Let R be a ring and let M be an abelian group.

item.title: Oriented equivalence
item.description: Let A be a set and take its orientation closure \vec{A} together with the action of e^{i\pi \mathbb{Z}}.

item.title: Principal Integral Domain (PID)
item.description: A non-zero ring R that does not contain any non-zero zero-divisors, and where every ideal is generated by a single element, is called a principal integral domain.

item.description: Let R be a ring and I\ideal R an ideal.

item.title: Rings
item.description: A ring is a structure of the type (R,+,\cdot,0,1) where R is a set (called carrier) upon which we can perform the binary operations: +,\cdot: R\times R\mapsto R called, respectively, addition and multiplication; 0,1 are distinct elements of R.
